subject: Discovery: Private deployment gaps + acceptance criteria (MedicaHealth)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Joan Ellis <joan.ellis@medicahealth.com>, Darren Lowe <darren.lowe@medicahealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0500
Subject: Discovery recap + proposed next steps (Private/VPC)

Hi Joan + Darren —

Thanks again for a productive 45-minute call this morning. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the success criteria you called out, and our proposed next steps. I want to make sure we captured everything accurately before Vivek and Priyom start mapping technical requirements.

Key pain points you emphasized:
- Must host inference inside MedicaHealth VPCs due to PHI handling and internal policy (no tokenized PHI leaves environment).
- Existing vendor endpoints fail internal vulnerability scans; need proof of network isolation + auditability.
- KMS ownership: encryption keys must be customer-managed (BYOK) with HSM-backed KMS and key rotation controls.
- Air-gap requirement on certain batch workflows (offline model scoring for archived records).

Current stack + constraints you shared:
- EKS (k8s 1.25) in AWS us-east-1, private subnets only, strict egress blocked except via NAT; no public IPs for endpoints.
- SAML SSO (Okta) and SCIM provisioning for service accounts.
- Internal SIEM: logs must be forwarded to Splunk over TLS and include per-request identifiers.
- Procurement: standard SOW + SOC 2 evidence required, and procurement lead expects contract slack of 30 days for reviews.

Success criteria (what MedicaHealth will evaluate in POC):
1) Network & isolation: Redwood deployed in our VPC with demonstrable peering/ENI model, traffic restricted to allowlist IPs, and ability to run without internet egress for inference path.
2) Crypto: Customer-managed KMS integration (AWS KMS custom key or HSM) with key control retained by MedicaHealth; HSM-backed keys preferred.
3) Auditability: Per-request audit logs (request id, model version, latency, tokens) delivered to our Splunk instance; retention policy configurable.
4) Functional: End-to-end latency p95 < 350ms for 128-token generative responses under dedicated capacity baseline; throughput target 100 qps sustained for initial phase.
5) Security posture: FIPS-compatible crypto options and ability to run in air-gapped batch mode for offline scoring jobs.

Proposed next steps (timeline):
- Action: Vivek + Priyom to draft a technical gap matrix and deployment options (VPC peering vs. PrivateLink vs. ENI) — deliver by Tue 11/17.
- Action: Joan to share network allowlist CSV and procurement contacts (done: procurement@medicahealth.com) — requested by Mon 11/16.
- Action: We will provision a scoped PoC plan (2-week) that demonstrates key items 1–3; draft SOW to follow.

Attachments: I attached a short scoping sheet (medica_scoping_sheet.xlsx) and a network allowlist template to speed collection.

If I've missed anything or mis-phrased a requirement, please flag and we'll correct. Otherwise we'll proceed with the gap matrix and PoC plan.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

[attachment: medica_scoping_sheet.xlsx (xlsx) — brief template with environment details]

From: Joan Ellis <joan.ellis@medicahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Darren Lowe <darren.lowe@medicahealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@medicahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:24:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + proposed next steps (Private/VPC)

Thanks Hannah — this is a great summary and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and extra items from our side:

Clarifications:
- The air-gap requirement applies only to nightly batch scoring for archived records (no network access during job execution). For online inference, we can allow egress to Redwood if it runs inside our VPC and does not traverse public internet.
- KMS: we use AWS KMS with custom key material (imported into KMS backed by an HSM). We will need a clear diagram of how keys are used during inference and where they reside.

Additional items to capture:
- Pen test / vulnerability scans: our security team will run a scan on the PoC environment; please confirm you can accommodate a scan window and share expected scan scope.
- Data residency: logs containing PHI must never be persisted outside our account; aggregated telemetry without PHI is acceptable to Redwood for product metrics.

Acceptable acceptance test for latency: we can be pragmatic — p95 < 400ms for 128 tokens during PoC is acceptable; production target should aim for p95 < 300ms.

I've shared the network allowlist template and a contact in procurement (procurement@medicahealth.com). We'll expect the PoC SOW for review; target start is week of 11/29 if SOW is signed and procurement clears it.

One small ask: does Redwood support an on-prem kube deployment (air-gapped) if we elect to host completely on-prem for PHI workloads? We might start with VPC but want options.

Joan
Director of Platform Security
MedicaHealth

[attachment: network_allowlist_template.csv (csv) — IP ranges and CIDR fields]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap + proposed next steps (MedicaHealth) — internal action list

Quick internal note after Joan's clarifications:

1) PoC scope: focus on VPC-native deployment (ENI model) with logs forwarded to their Splunk instance; include a plan for air-gapped batch runner as an extension.
2) KMS flow: Priyom please draft a short diagram showing key import -> usage -> rotation for AWS KMS + HSM compatibility by EOD Mon (11/16).
3) Pen test readiness: Vivek to add a one-page scan scope doc and expected timeslots; confirm support for customer-initiated scans.
4) Procurement: once Joan confirms SOW timeline (wk of 11/29) we should accelerate SOW draft this week; I'll loop Sales Ops for redlines.

I'll coordinate with Product to confirm whether we can offer an on-prem kube artifact for fully air-gapped installs — flagging as "possible but longer lead time".

Attachments for internal: md-deploy-checklist.pdf (internal checklist) — use it to map deliverables against acceptance criteria.

Hannah
